title: Real-time bioluminescence imaging of myeloperoxidase activity in small laboratory animals
protocol: Make a stock solution of luminol by dissolving luminol sodium salt powder in PBS to a final concentration of 50 mg/mL.
Filter the luminol stock solution through a 0.2 μm filter.
Aliquot filtered luminol into sterile Eppendorf tubes and store at -20°C.
Make a stock solution of PMA by dissolving PMA in ethanol to a final concentration of 100 μM.
Aliquot PMA stock solution and store at -20°C.
Select mice for the experiment one week prior to starting.
Place selected mice into cages with minimal numbers (≤3) per cage.
Anesthetize the mice using isoflurane inhalation (2% isoflurane/98% oxygen).
Verify that outlets leading to the imaging system are closed if applicable.
Check that the mice are well anesthetized by foot or tail pinching.
Topically apply PMA (100 μM, 20 μL) to the left ear of each mouse using a clean cotton swab and gloves.
Topically apply vehicle (ethanol, 20 μL) to the right ear of each mouse using a clean cotton swab and gloves.
Number each mouse on the tail using a waterproof marker.
Allow all mice to recover for 24-48 hours after PMA application.
Open the LivingImage software installed on the IVIS 100 instrument.
Initialize the system.
Ensure that the stage is equilibrated to 37°C.
Place a sheet of black paper on the stage of the IVIS system.
Thaw enough luminol stock solution for the number of mice planned for imaging.
Calculate the volume needed for a dose of 200 mg/kg body weight.
Fill a 1 mL syringe equipped with a 27 gauge needle with sufficient luminol solution to image a single mouse.
Anesthetize the mouse in the anesthesia tank using isoflurane inhalation.
After the mouse is anesthetized, check by pinching.
Rapidly weigh the mouse and place an open anesthesia outlet on its nose.
Record the weight of the mouse.
Inject the luminol solution intraperitoneally (i.p.).
Immediately start the timer after injecting the luminol solution.
Move the mouse to the IVIS 100 imaging system.
Place the mouse on its abdomen on the black sheet with the anesthesia port positioned on its snout.
Using LivingImage software and instrument commands, move the stage to position A (FOV 7.5 cm).
Adjust the position of the mouse so that its head will be at the center of the image.
Record a few sequential images of the mouse while adjusting its position with luminescence turned off.
Optional: affix the mouse's feet to the black sheet using 1 cm pieces of black Scotch tape after proper positioning.
Set the acquisition parameters as follows: luminescence on, exposure time 180 sec, binning 4, FOV 7.5 cm.
Begin acquiring a bioluminescence image set ten minutes after i.p. injection of luminol.
Save the image and open the door of the IVIS 100.
Remove the tape from the mouse and allow it to recover in its cage.
Repeat steps for each mouse to be imaged.
If results need to be compared to histology, euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation.
Cut the ear lobes from their base using surgical scissors and place them in pre-marked vials containing 10% neutral formalin buffer.
Use LivingImage software tools to draw three oval regions-of-interest over the images of the ears and on the center of the skull.
Place one ROI on each earlobe and use the rotation tool for appropriate positioning.
Measure the photon fluxes in each ROI using the LivingImage software.
Record the results.
